question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own a durable AI-safety event store, operator UI, and public plugin manifest/API for third-party safety-event emission, or should the work be narrowed to existing diagnostics/plugin seams?
rationale: This is a new cross-cutting product and plugin-SDK contract with persistence and security-provenance consequences; source review cannot determine the intended permanent scope without maintainer direction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Define the supported event families, provenance visibility, retention behavior, and external-plugin permission model, then require a rebased implementation and real runtime proof.

options.title: Keep events internal to diagnostics
options.body: Retain only core-owned diagnostic emission and exporter integration, while deferring the public plugin API, persistent history, and Control UI until separately approved.

options.title: Route extension behavior outside core
options.body: Keep OpenClaw’s existing diagnostics seams and move optional safety dashboards or third-party event producers into plugins after confirming no core API gap remains.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define the supported event families, provenance visibility, retention behavior, and external-plugin permission model, then require a rebased implementation and real runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the current owners of diagnostics, plugin SDK, state storage, Gateway, and Control UI; the supplied review material does not establish a single named owner.
